roasts.title: Roast My TechStack #6

speakers.name: Gaurav Kumar Manek
speakers.summary: Five grader types for LLM output — exact match, code execution, trajectory checks, LLM judge, human review — with a rule to prefer the cheapest grader that catches the failure mode. Warned against ungrounded, agent-authored output ('shipping fiction').

keyTakeaways: Grade at the top of the ladder first: each rung down costs more and catches less.
Fail-continue rather than fail-fast in parallel content pipelines — keep partial success, retry only what broke.
Workflows are deterministic; agents figure out the path — keep paths fixed where possible.
Imagen is cheaper but can't render text in images; GPT Image can.
discussionPoints: Parallel content generation: one input to podcast, blog, images, audio in parallel
Imagen vs. GPT Image for text-in-image generation
Deterministic n8n workflows vs. goal-driven agents

roasts.title: Roast My TechStack #3

speakers.name: Gaurav Murarka
speakers.summary: Walked through the counter-intuitive storage mechanism of his previous startup Visigoth.ai and the structure that worked best. Slides public at github.com/gauravmm/2026-04-Roast-My-Tech-Stack.

keyTakeaways: Counter-intuitive storage structures can beat 'textbook' designs in practice depending on scale.
Trade-offs that make a wrong-looking design the right one don't always generalise.
discussionPoints: What generalises beyond the product's specific shape

roasts.title: Roast My TechStack #2

speakers.name: Ee One Lim
speakers.summary: App that teaches Spanish through music. Stack: Claude for planning/coding, Google Stitch via MCP for design, YouTube for music, LRCLib for lyrics, Gemini for translations.

keyTakeaways: Fixes from the room: lyrics-syncing bug, model-specific issues, security and scalability architecture changes.
Vibe-coded AI stacks can ship fast but accumulate architecture debt.
discussionPoints: Security and scalability before growing user base
